I enjoy building software that solves real problems, from understanding requirements and shaping data to implementation, testing, and delivering a usable product.

caseStudy.title: From fragmented approvals to an accountable workflow
caseStudy.intro: The product was designed around a real organizational problem: requests lose context when they move between paper, PDFs, and email threads. The solution centralizes the request, evaluates the applicable route, records every decision, and keeps each role focused on the work it can actually perform.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: Internal purchase, leave, expense, and travel requests need consistent routing, visible ownership, and an audit record. Email chains make status and accountability difficult to recover.
items: One source of truth for every request
Clear current step and next owner
A chronological record of state changes

sections.title: The product model
sections.body: Each company runs its own centrally hosted instance and SQL Server database. Employees submit structured requests; the approval engine selects a published workflow or safe fallback path using request type, amount, branch, and department.
items: Manager, role, employee, and department approvers

sections.title: Engineering decisions
sections.body: Business rules live behind the API rather than in presentation-only conditions. Permission policies protect endpoints, domain transitions reject invalid state changes, and secure cookies plus CSRF validation protect authenticated writes.

sections.title: Delivery and verification
sections.body: The system includes unit, integration, frontend, and Playwright coverage. The portfolio media comes from the guarded E2E environment using fake company data and role-specific sessions, never from a fabricated dashboard.

caseStudy.title: Private personal finance without account friction
caseStudy.intro: Masroofi began from a client request for a direct Iraqi money-tracking experience. The product avoids account setup and remote storage: transactions stay in the browser, the balance is always calculated from the ledger, and the user controls portable backups.

sections.title: The request
sections.body: The core need was simple: record money coming in and going out, understand the current balance immediately, and keep the interface familiar to an Arabic-speaking user.

sections.title: Local-first data model
sections.body: A single transaction model stores income and expenses in IndexedDB. Totals and balance are derived rather than duplicated, reducing the risk of stored values drifting apart.
items: Indexed indexes for date and type
Immediate UI updates after each write

sections.title: Safety and portability
sections.body: Backup files are versioned and validated before they can change the ledger. Restore offers an explicit choice between merging compatible records and replacing the existing history.
items: Portable JSON owned by the user

sections.title: Product polish
sections.body: The final experience includes a custom date-time picker, optional emojis, light, dark, and system themes, reduced-motion behavior, responsive navigation, and an installable PWA shell.
